title: which of E521's undecidable arms becomes decidable when the guard's argument is followed one hop into the caller
population_source: e527_undecidable_arm.py::population() -- E521's published sites whose verdict is exactly 'raises and the arm's reachability is not decidable from the call site'
method_limits: one hop only: a name the caller binds from a call result or from its own parameter is published as still open rather than followed further

a literal binding is accepted only when it dominates the call -- a binding inside an if/for/while/try that the call does not itself sit in, and a name bound more than once before the call, both stay open
the guard parameter is taken from the same first-parameter-naming `if` walk E521 used, so a parameter published here is the parameter E521's reach class named
an arm behind a test that names no parameter of the callee is published as structural: following an argument cannot settle an arm that does not read the call

a name the caller function never binds is looked up once in the module scope: a module-level literal settles the arm, any other module binding is published as module-scope-only rather than as an unbound name
nothing is executed and no source is rewritten
sources_read is a snapshot of a live tree other lanes write to; it is published but not gated, while every class, every outcome and the verdict are re-derived
